metadata.title: BATU CAVES & PETALING Street Food Tour : Nasi Lemak, Nasi Kerabu, Chee Chong Fun, Kaya Toast
metadata.description:
In today’s episode, we embark on an exciting journey through Kuala Lumpur, starting with a visit to the iconic Batu Caves, alongside our knowledgeable host, Siddoz. Nestled within a limestone hill, Batu Cave Temple is one of the most revered Hindu shrines outside India, dedicated to Lord Murugan. As we made our way up the 272 colorful steps leading to the caves, we were surrounded by vibrant murals and statues, immersing us in the spiritual energy of the place. The towering golden statue of Lord Murugan and the serene, natural beauty of the caves made the experience all the more awe-inspiring.

From this sacred site, we transitioned to a vibrant and flavour-packed food tour of Petaling Street, starting with a stop at Nasi Lemak Wanjo in Kampung Baru. Here, we tried nasi lemak, a beloved Malaysian dish. The rice, cooked in coconut milk and pandan leaves, was wonderfully fragrant and served with a side of sambal, fried anchovies, boiled eggs, cucumber, and tender chicken. The combination of flavors and textures made this classic dish truly unforgettable.

Our next stop was Kak Som, also located in Kampung Baru, where we were introduced to nasi kerabu. This traditional Malaysian rice dish is known for its striking blue color, thanks to the butterfly pea flower used in the cooking process. The dish was served with fish sauce, sambal, and crunchy fish crackers, offering a perfect balance of savory and spicy flavors.

The food adventure continued as we arrived at Toast Master in the City Centre, a popular spot for a classic Malaysian snack, kaya butter toast. The crispy toast, smeared with a rich coconut spread (kaya) and butter, was both simple and indulgent. We paired this with a local favorite beverage, cham, which is a strong and delicious mix of tea, condensed milk, and coffee.

Next, we visited Yooi Kee Chee Cheong Fun on Jalan Petaling, where we tried chee cheong fun, a dish of soft, steamed rice noodle rolls topped with sambal, fermented soybean sauce, and sesame seeds. The combination of the silky noodles and the punchy sauces created an explosion of flavors in every bite.

Our final stop was at Air Mata Kucing on Jalan Hang Lekir, where we refreshed ourselves with the namesake drink, air mata kucing. This cooling beverage, made of longan, monk fruit, sugar, and water, was the perfect way to end our food tour, leaving us feeling rejuvenated.
